summary: Reserve notice source, snapshot and control namespaces and reviewed registration hashes before enabling notice facts.

replay.detail: Projection version 2 rebuilds custom registration and source caches once on ordinary upgrade, rejecting pre-reservation substitute manifests even on quiet databases. Authoritative claims and documents remain intact; downgrade recovery may require replay.

schema.detail: Adds three compiled v1 custom storage manifests with exact serialized-byte SHA256 pins.

rules.detail: Reserved prefixes, prefix ancestors and notice claim kinds cannot be registered with substitute manifests. Reserved fact writes remain unavailable in this slice.

compatibility.detail: Generic custom, claim, history, event, status and replication-diagnostic readers isolate reserved subjects or claim kinds before disclosure. Generic status and full typed status selectors exclude contaminated subjects before reduction. Native agent cards and terminal cards instead retain agents while stripping reserved rows before field, source and provenance reduction; pagination membership and cold-roster completion use the same native inputs, with serving caches isolated from internal reductions. Claim/history pages fill from visible rows. Custom basis and keyed client history/status refuse reserved resources. Legacy reserved rows cannot poison unrelated direct or cached attention. Full-state backup, rename-proof export and member replication retain complete authoritative bytes for restore/proof integrity. Paired clients are refused these transfer routes on every platform; ancestry-bound agents are refused on Linux only. Non-Linux ancestry binding is absent and agent transfer containment there is not established. This does not provide native recipient-authorized notice reads.

manual.detail: No notice publication is enabled by this change.

recovery.detail: Restore the reviewed manifest, not a substitute registration. Reservation metadata reads are batched rather than probing each subject. Projection invalidation clears serving and internal card/view caches together, preserving canonical card revisions after repair. Test-support blocking reads retain their fixture's frozen delivery clocks; production assessment scheduling is unchanged. Replicated admission ordering and revocation provenance remain a separate change.
